The restrictions are substantive. The new sampler requires $\eta_z=0$ and an explicit constant bound on $JT$. It does not construct the requested positive $\eta_{\mathrm{sample}}$, and it cannot be iterated to cover arbitrary time by treating a sampled measurement record as the next quantum preparation. I also did not obtain a model-preserving sampling-hardness reduction.

The complete mathematical return, including proofs, costs, failure examples and source boundaries, is saved here:

1. The completed restricted sampler

Here is the precise new positive result.

Expand each local Hamiltonian term into at most $4^k$ Pauli terms, and put

$$d_{\mathrm P}=4^k d.$$

Each resulting coefficient has magnitude at most $J$. In each schedule segment, color the term-conflict graph with at most

$$c=kd_{\mathrm P}$$

colors, padding segments to the same declared number of colors.

Choose fixed connected lattice balls containing the terms assigned to each anchor. Let $s$ bound their size, $h$ their cover multiplicity, and $\ell_0\ge1$ their diameter. These constants are computable from the fixed locality class.

A conservative sufficient time condition is

$$\boxed{\quad
JT\le \frac{1}{24shd_{\mathrm P}c}.
\quad} \tag{1}$$

Theorem. Under (1), the native unital process

$$\mathcal L_t=-i[H(t),\cdot]+\gamma\sum_i(E_i-\mathrm{Id})$$

admits an unconditional TV-$\epsilon$ sampler for the entire supplied one-site POVM output law, with worst-case bit work

$$\boxed{\quad
\operatorname{poly}_{a,k,d}
\!\left(n,B,1+g^{-1},\epsilon^{-1}\right).
\quad} \tag{2}$$

It covers every supplied rational product preparation and every rational piecewise Hamiltonian schedule satisfying the declared bounds. The schedule, output lists, arithmetic, truncations and random bits are included.

This is a proved and costed mathematical algorithm using the accepted finite-bit MPS primitive. I have not executed new general sampler software.

1. Replica cancellation and amplification

The cancellation is valid.

For a connected component $X$, every doubled local generator supported in $X$ commutes with the swap of the two $X$ registers. Its connected kernel $K_X$ therefore does also. The initial product replica vector is invariant under every such swap.

After applying the same rank-one measurement bra to both copies of $B$, a swap on $X\subseteq A\cup B$ becomes a swap on $A\cap X$. For a retained disjoint component family, the components intersecting $A$, together with uncovered sites of $A$, partition $A$. The resulting vector is invariant under their product, namely $\mathrm{Swap}_A$. This proves its annihilation by $P_A^-$.

The norm argument needs—and the revised text explicitly uses—the fully amplified word-norm majorants. An individual local term

$$-i(H_\alpha\otimes I+I\otimes H_\alpha)$$

has projective-norm operator bound $2\|H_\alpha\|$ even with arbitrary untouched spatial registers. Products of words consequently have the required product bounds. The restricted exterior is $U_{\rm restricted}\otimes U_{\rm restricted}$, with norm one. No unamplified-to-amplified norm equivalence is being assumed.

I also checked the rank-one measurement map. Its projective-to-$\ell^1$-Hilbert contraction follows directly from completeness and Cauchy–Schwarz. Partial swap is used only as a Hilbert-norm contraction, so no problematic projective-norm bound for partial swap is required.
